rows.title: GOP to Lamont: Take Biden to court to expand tax relief for CT residents
rows.standfirst: Republicans want CT to join other states in challenging federal rules that limit the state’s ability to cut taxes this year.

rows.title: Audit: West Haven misspent $893,000 in federal relief funding
rows.standfirst: Officials are considering a takeover of West Haven’s finances after an audit found the city misspent federal pandemic relief funding.

rows.title: State unions ratify contracts granting raises and $3,500 bonuses
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont will ask lawmakers to approve large bonuses as workers retire from state government in increasing numbers.

rows.title: Tax relief expected to dominate CT legislature’s budget plan this week
rows.standfirst: Lawmakers are expected to endorse income tax cuts for the working poor and middle class, as well as a new child tax credit.

rows.title: Lamont defends deal with state employees as way to preserve services
rows.standfirst: The deal allows state workers to collect 70% of their bonuses and still retire before more stringent pension benefits kick in July 1.

rows.title: Lawmakers move closer to new tax break for families with kids
rows.standfirst: The bill would create a new $600-per-child credit for low and middle income families.

rows.title: Lawmakers challenge Lamont to go bigger on property tax relief
rows.standfirst: The Finance Committee approved bills that increase – and broaden – property and child tax credits for Connecticut residents.

rows.title: Committee passes $24.2 billion budget to push CT past pandemic
rows.standfirst: The plan makes unprecedented new investments in child care while fully funding the state’s contracting watchdog agency for the first time.

rows.title: Lamont urges lawmakers not to overreach on tax cuts
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont advised lawmakers to “follow the rules of the road” by sticking with budgetary safety net they established in 2017.

rows.title: CT officials vote to increase state control over West Haven’s finances
rows.standfirst: The Municipal Accountability Review Board voted to tighten its grip over West Haven’s spending even as the city’s leaders objected.

rows.title: Report: State workers’ raises would cost almost $1.9 billion over four years
rows.standfirst: The package, which would force CT to draw almost $300 million from its reserves, is expected to come under fire from Republican lawmakers.

rows.title: Budget panel braces for intense hearing on CT employee raises and bonuses
rows.standfirst: The Appropriations Committee hearing will address an issue that has polarized the General Assembly, labor and taxpayer advocacy groups.

rows.title: Budget panel endorses raises, bonuses for CT state workers
rows.standfirst: The Appropriations Committee endorsed raises and bonuses that would boost compensation for most state employees by 7% this year.

rows.title: An unusual event: CT legislature to vote on raises for state workers
rows.standfirst: Top legislative leaders announced they expect to wrap voting on a major new package of raises and bonuses for state employees by week’s end.

rows.title: CT budget surplus nears $4 billion; lawmakers push for tax relief
rows.standfirst: With almost $7 billion in budget reserves, CT legislators are waiting impatiently for Gov. Ned Lamont to agree on a child tax credit.

rows.title: GOP pitches income tax cut, says CT can’t sit on $7 billion in reserves
rows.standfirst: Republican lawmakers unveiled a $1.2 billion tax relief plan, including what would be the first income tax rate reduction in 27 years.

rows.title: House passes raises, bonuses for CT state employees
rows.standfirst: The Democrat-controlled House voted 96-52 to approve the contracts after a 4-hour debate. The Senate is expected to ratify the deal Friday.

rows.title: Surging revenues could solve Democrats’ tax-cutting dilemma
rows.standfirst: Lamont and legislators could have a budget deal hammered out over the weekend.

rows.title: Social service agencies see big raises for unions and ask: Why not us?
rows.standfirst: As state budget talks wind down, CT nonprofits ask why a $72 million proposal to help their industry, which employs 115,000, is bogged down.

rows.title: Senate gives final approval to raises, bonuses for CT state employees
rows.standfirst: The Democratic-controlled Senate voted 22-13 along party lines to approve the contracts, which cover about 46,000 workers.

rows.title: Lamont, legislators on the cusp of a new CT budget deal
rows.standfirst: Legislative leaders and Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration have offered compromises, and debate and a vote could be as soon as this weekend.

rows.title: CT budget deal includes $600M in tax cuts, extends gas tax holiday
rows.standfirst: Gov. Ned Lamont and legislative leaders have agreed on a new $24 billion state budget that features nearly $600 million in tax cuts.

rows.title: House balks at proposal to privatize delinquent tax collection
rows.standfirst: Legislators want more information next year from Gov. Ned Lamont’s administration on its plan to sell CT tax debt.
